items.t: CVT automatic transmission failure
items.job: Replace CVT with a used or remanufactured unit
items.note: A good used unit is the cheapest route; a new unit from the dealer costs far more.

items.t: Early 5-speed manual gearbox failure
items.job: Replace manual transmission (used or later-style unit)
items.note: Converting to the later Getrag gearbox may need extra parts.

items.t: Power steering pump overheating or failing
items.job: Replace electro-hydraulic power steering pump and fan
items.note: Used and remanufactured pumps cost less than new.

items.t: Loss of power steering assist (recall)
items.note: Free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Cracked coolant expansion tank
items.job: Replace coolant expansion tank and cap

items.t: Oil leaks from crank sensor seal and front main seal
items.job: Replace crank sensor O-ring or front main seal
items.note: The crank sensor O-ring is the quick job; the front main seal takes longer.

items.t: Clutch wearing out early
items.job: Replace clutch kit (flywheel extra if needed)
items.note: A dual-mass flywheel can add several hundred dollars.

items.t: Passenger airbag turned off by faulty seat sensor (recall)
items.note: Free at a dealer. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Timing chain rattle on cold start
items.job: Replace timing chain, guides and tensioner
items.note: Fitting only the updated tensioner is much cheaper if caught early.

items.t: High-pressure fuel pump failure
Carbon buildup on intake valves
Turbo oil feed line leak and turbo failure
items.note: If the turbo has already failed, expect $1,500-$3,000 more.

items.t: Valve cover gasket oil seep

Water pump and thermostat housing coolant leaks
items.job: Replace water pump and thermostat housing

items.t: Electric water pump or coolant hose failure (2.0L turbo)
